leads.summary: History replay turns an explicitly timed critical toast into a permanent popup
leads.consequence: A critical -t 30000 toast now expires and enters history, but opening notification history replays that entry with critical urgency and expireTimeout=0. durationFor(Critical,0)=0, so the replay never ages out; it requires a manual dismissal. The same happens to a still-visible timed critical toast carried into showHistory. The existing test calls this the 'standard toast lifetime' even though it is infinite for this new category.
leads.triage: behavioural_opus_followup; Opus followup-1 Q1: replay lifetime 0 at base and head; not a regression; not published

leads.summary: In-place escalation to timed critical can expire almost immediately
leads.consequence: With a normal toast 7.9 s into its 8 s lifetime (remainingLifetime approximately 0.0125), a replaces_id update that changes only urgency to Critical and expireTimeout to 30000 rewrites the model, but does not reset remainingLifetime. The new critical lifetime is 30 s yet the old fractional remainder gives it about 375 ms on screen, not a full 8-30 s to notice the escalation. A sender can use -p/-r to update without changing summary/body/image.
leads.triage: behavioural_opus_followup_confirmed; Opus followup-1 Q2: introduced by first commit, narrow, no in-repo sender; published as narrowed correction of 'in-place updates unchanged'

leads.summary: Open timeout PRs can undo the floor or revive immortal first-party timed alerts if integrated without reconciling their duration branches
leads.location: open PR #13159 (ad42197a) shell/plugins/notifications/Service.qml:102-106; open PR #13041 (e91ca658) Service.qml:102-108; open PR #12964 (2fc20a79) Service.qml:102-110
leads.consequence: If #13159's critical branch supersedes this PR's branch during integration, any omarchy-action or notify-send critical toast remains permanent even with -t 30000, reinstating the low-battery restore problem; #13041 or #12964 instead loses the 8 s floor (and #13041 also loses the 30 s cap), reverting F1 for the 3000/5000 ms screen-recording alerts. This is a conditional integration conflict, not a failure of the pinned head alone.
leads.triage: factual_verified; Coordinator read #13159 keepsCriticalOnScreen and omarchy-notification-send default app_name=omarchy-action; Opus merge-tree confirmed conflicts; corroborates Opus N2; published as Related open PRs note

leads.summary: Open PR #13161's policy refactor makes this PR's new source-regex assertion fail if both changes are kept
leads.consequence: #13161 moves durationFor policy into NotificationLogic.js and replaces the entire Critical switch branch in Service.qml with a one-line call, while this PR adds a test that explicitly requires the now-absent branch text. Merging both behavioral changes while leaving this test unchanged fails notifications-test.sh even though the intended positive critical timeout policy still works; test needs migration to behavioral assertions for the JS helper.
leads.triage: factual_verified; #13161 Service.qml durationFor delegates to NotificationLogic; published as one clause

## Automated AI review

> **Community review:** Independent automated community review, unaffiliated with the Omarchy team, intended to help prepare PRs for their review.

Follow-up to the [earlier review](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/pull/13100#issuecomment-5825488051) (at 6b95224d) and the [author's reply](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/pull/13100#issuecomment-5825679160), checked at head 2d19a2e1.

**Verified:** 2d19a2e1 and the edited PR description resolve the short-critical-timeout finding, the stale documentation and the PR description's spec rationale. The optional test improvement still applies. No regression from 2d19a2e1 was found, and the #12911 fix still holds: the issue's persisted battery toast (critical, 30000 ms, 18 h old) is archived on restore.

| Earlier note | Status at 2d19a2e1 |
|---|---|
| Short critical timeouts are the shortest-lived toasts | Resolved |
| Documentation (`docs/notifications.md`, `popupExpired()` comment, test label) | Resolved |
| Rationale wording in the PR description | Resolved |
| Optional test improvement (source regex) | Still applies |

**Verified, short critical timeouts:** the critical branch of `durationFor()` now uses the suggested floor:

```text
durationFor(Critical, requested) at 2d19a2e1
  1 .. 7999 ms   -> 8000 ms   (normal floor)
  8000 .. 29999  -> as requested
  >= 30000       -> 30000 ms  (cap)
  -1, 0          -> 0         (until dismissed, unchanged)
```

Low and normal results are identical at base, the earlier head and this head.

**Correction to the earlier sender table:** the three screen-recording rows no longer hold. `bin/omarchy-capture-screenrecording` (lines 26, 79 and 234) and `bin/omarchy-capture-screenrecording-with-webcam` request 3000 or 5000 ms and now show for 8 s, not 3 or 5 s. The `bin/omarchy-battery-low` row (30 s) still holds. The earlier remark that a 3 s critical error "matches that earlier behavior" also no longer holds: under mako those errors showed for 3 s. Parity with mako now covers requests from 8 to 30 s, and the PR description states the floor and the cap.

**Verified, documentation:** `docs/notifications.md` (Toast lifecycle), the comment above `popupExpired()` and the test label now limit "never expires" to critical alerts sent without a timeout, matching the code.

**Verified, rationale:** the PR description now rests on the sender's explicit request and the earlier mako behavior, with no spec-violation claim. The message of commit 6b95224d still presents honoring a non-zero timeout "regardless of urgency" as what the freedesktop spec says. That sentence enters history if the commit is merged as is.

**Optional test improvement (still applies):** the updated assertion is still a regex over the `Service.qml` source. It fails on the base and earlier-head code, so it pins the new expression. It still passes when `requested` is forced to 0, which brings #12911 back, and when `restorePopups()` is given duration 0. It fails a behavior-identical rewrite of the expression. Moving the duration policy into `NotificationLogic.js`, as suggested earlier, would allow behavioral tests (for example critical 3000 gives 8000, 30000 gives 30000, 0/-1 gives 0, 60000 gives 30000, and `popupExpired()` is true for the issue's 18 h old entry). Those would catch the forced-zero case and accept equivalent rewrites. The `restorePopups()` call site would still need its own check.

**Related open PRs:** #12964, #13041, #13159, #13161 and #8675 also edit the critical branch of `durationFor()`, so they will conflict with this PR. In #13159, critical alerts from `omarchy-action` keep lifetime 0. `omarchy-action` is the default app name of `omarchy-notification-send`, which `omarchy-battery-low` uses, so resolving the conflict toward #13159 would make the battery toast permanent again. #12964 and #13041 pass short critical timeouts through without the 8 s floor. #13161 moves the policy into `NotificationLogic.js`, where this PR's source regex would no longer match.

**Narrower earlier statement, in-place updates:** the earlier review listed in-place updates as unchanged. One narrow case changed from the first commit on. A `replaces_id` update that keeps the summary, body and image but raises urgency to a timed critical now inherits the remaining fraction of the old countdown. For example, a normal toast with about 100 ms left, updated to critical `-t 30000`, closes about 400 ms later. At base it stayed until dismissed. Low and normal updates already rescale this way at base. The only in-repo `replaces_id` sender, `bin/omarchy-display-text-size`, sends low urgency without a timeout, so it never hits this case.

---

## Review information

**Test scope:** Source review of the incremental and full diff at 2d19a2e1, the notification service, `NotificationLogic.js`, the in-repo critical senders, the docs, the related open PRs, the freedesktop specification 1.3, Quickshell v0.3.1 and mako v1.11.0. In an isolated sandbox with Node, `test/shell.d/notifications-test.sh` passed at head. The head test failed only its new assertion on the base and earlier-head code. Mutation runs covered forced-zero `requested`, a zero restore duration and an equivalent rewrite. A harness ran `durationFor()`, `requestedDuration()` and `restorePopups()` verbatim from each revision, with the real `NotificationLogic.js`: 835 checks, 0 mismatches against predictions. A second harness modeled history replay and the card's countdown on in-place updates. The live shell, the QML engine and D-Bus were not run, so the on-screen countdown, hover pause and close signalling were not observed.
